label: copy-phase input b (echo of original token at position >=2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is b, i.e. the model is re-reading an original b at original position >= 2 (recall_idx >= 3). It never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, even on b. It almost never fires on other input tokens (fewer than 25 steps per token). Copy-phase b echoing original position 1 (recall_idx 2) fires only weakly and inconsistently (rate about 0.007, activations around 0.02-0.16 of max); echoing position 0 does not fire at all. These weak cases are about 1% of activation mass. Magnitude is strongest when the input b comes right after another b (bb runs, 0.7-1.0 of max) and is typically 0.3-0.5 of max for an isolated b. Rare false positives are b at original position 2 in some contexts.

issues: The predicate reproduces on test: P=0.999, R=0.939, F1=0.968, mass recall 0.989. Every activation is in the copy phase (phase 0 and the delimiter step: 0 active). All other input tokens together give precision 5e-5 and 0.02% of mass. The worst single token is z with 22 dev steps, which fits the 'fewer than 25 per token' claim.

The misses are what the explanation says they are. Of the 3753 missed test steps, the ones shown are all copy-phase b at recall_idx 2 (echoing original position 1), at about 0.01-0.07 of max, together 1.1% of mass. The predicate b & recall_idx==2 has precision 0.22, which fits 'weak and inconsistent'. The 78 false positives look like scattered noise: b at recall_idx 3, mostly in L=7-8 sequences.

The explanation leaves out the main magnitude effect, which is a ramp with original position. Mean activation per active step (mass recall / recall) is about 0.64 at recall_idx 3, 1.06 at 4, and 1.31 at >=6, roughly a 2x rise. It also rises toward the end of the sequence. This is an omission, not a counterexample.

The bb claim is somewhat overstated. Holding position fixed (recall_idx>=5), b after b has a relative mean of 1.54 versus 1.29 for an isolated b, only about a 1.2x boost. bb steps hold just 3.9% of mass. The top examples are bb, but an average bb is around 0.6 of max, not consistently 0.7-1.0.
No systematic false-positive or miss class remains beyond the documented weak recall_idx==2 cases. The label matches the predicate.
